transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you here today?

Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve been getting really fixated on my face, especially the left side. It looks uneven and kind of puffy to me, like on video calls or in photos from salsa, and I know people tell me they don’t see it, so I feel a little silly even saying it.

But I keep noticing it, and it’s been starting to affect work calls and going out socially more than I’d like. I’m not sure if that’s the right kind of thing to bring up, but… it’s been bothering me.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or self-conscious in social situations, especially where others might be paying attention to your appearance?

Yeah… I do, especially if I think my face is sort of on display. Like on work video calls, I’ll get really aware of the left side of my face and whether it looks uneven or puffy. And with salsa photos, I can end up feeling embarrassed, even though people keep telling me they don’t notice anything.

I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is, but it has started to affect how comfortable I feel at work and going out socially. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you spend a lot of time thinking about the way your face looks, or do these concerns interfere with your daily activities, like work or spending time with friends?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to overstate it, because I am still functioning mostly, but it does take up more time than I’d like.

There have been times I’ve missed ticket deadlines at work or joined video calls late because I was sort of stuck checking how my face looked and couldn’t quite get past it. My supervisor actually brought it up in a performance review, which was embarrassing.

And socially… I’ve skipped some salsa nights and community events if I knew people were probably going to be taking photos. I know that probably sounds avoidant, but at the time it feels easier than dealing with seeing pictures afterward.
Do you find yourself being very critical of yourself in other areas of life, like work or hobbies, where things need to feel 'just right' or meet high standards?

Um… I’m not sure. I mean, I do try to do a good job at work, and I like things to be decent, but I don’t know if I’d say I’m extremely “just right” about everything.

Maybe I can be a little self-critical, but it doesn’t feel like the same kind of thing, if that makes sense. I haven’t really noticed it being a big pattern outside of the appearance stuff. Is that helpful, or am I answering that too vaguely?
When you’re worried about how your face looks, do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking mirrors, taking a lot of selfies, or trying to cover it up?

Yeah… I do some of that. I try not to, but before meetings or before going out I’ll open the camera preview a bunch of times, just to see how my face looks in the lighting.

Sometimes I’ll change the angle, move closer to a window, fix my hair around the side I’m worried about… and if I’m taking a photo, I might retake it several times. I’ve also asked friends, probably too many times, if I look strange or if that side looks noticeable.

It sounds kind of silly saying it out loud, but it can make me late, or by the time I’m done I feel too drained to even go. Is that the sort of repeated behavior you mean?
Outside of work and social situations, do you find that these concerns about your face affect other areas of your life, like your mood, relationships, or how you see yourself overall?

I guess… yes, in the sense that it spills over more than I’d like to admit. I try to keep it contained, but it’s affected how reliable I seem at work — like I’ve missed some ticket deadlines or joined video calls late because I couldn’t get past how I looked. My supervisor even mentioned it in a review, which was pretty mortifying.

And outside of work, I’ve skipped salsa nights or community events if I thought people would be taking photos. I tell myself it’s not a huge deal, like “it’s just one night,” but then it adds up, I guess. Does that answer what you mean?

When you’re worried about how your face looks, is it mainly the appearance of that specific area that bothers you, or is it more about how others might judge you in general during social interactions?

I think it’s mainly that specific area… the left side of my face. Like, I worry it looks uneven or puffy, especially on video calls or in photos from salsa nights.

I mean, I do worry what people will think, obviously, but it feels like that comes after I notice my face, if that makes sense. Everyone tells me they don’t really see what I’m talking about, so I know maybe I’m overfocusing on it, but I can’t seem to stop checking or thinking about it.

Sorry, is that the kind of distinction you mean?

When you look at the left side of your face and feel concerned, do you feel like it looks physically abnormal, unattractive, or even disfigured to the point that you feel there’s something wrong with how you look overall?

I… I don’t know if I’d say “disfigured,” exactly. That sounds really strong, and I know other people keep telling me they don’t see what I’m seeing.

But when I look at it, especially on video calls or in photos from salsa, the left side of my face just looks uneven and kind of puffy to me. It makes me feel like something is off with my whole face, like it’s the first thing anyone would notice. That’s honestly why I came in — I can’t seem to stop focusing on it, even though I’m trying to be reasonable about it.

When you're worried about your face, is your main concern that others will judge you negatively for how you look, or is it more about how the left side of your face doesn't look the way you feel it should, regardless of what others might think?

I think… it’s more the second one. I mean, I do worry people will judge me, of course, but the thing that starts it is that the left side of my face just doesn’t look right to me — like uneven or puffy, especially on video calls or in salsa photos.

And I know everyone keeps saying they don’t see anything, so I feel a little silly saying it out loud, but I came in because I can’t stop focusing on it. It’s starting to affect work and social stuff more than I’d like. Does that make sense?

When you look at the left side of your face and feel concerned, do you believe there's something visibly wrong or abnormal that others should also notice, or does it feel off to you even though others don’t seem to see it?

I guess… it feels visibly wrong to me, but I’m aware other people don’t seem to see it. Like, I’ll look at myself on a video call or in a photo from salsa and the left side just looks uneven and puffy, and then I can’t stop focusing on it.

I don’t want to sound dramatic, because everyone keeps saying they don’t notice anything, but to me it really stands out. It’s gotten to where it’s starting to interfere with work and social things a bit, which is why I thought I should come in. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you feel that the issue with the left side of your face is something that should be obvious to others, even though they don’t seem to notice it?

I think… part of me feels like it should be obvious, because when I see it on video calls or in those salsa photos, the left side looks so uneven and puffy to me. Like, I can’t understand how it wouldn’t stand out.

But then everyone keeps telling me they don’t see anything, so I’m trying not to insist that they should. I just know I can’t stop focusing on it, and it’s starting to affect work and social stuff more than I’d like. I’m sorry if I’m repeating myself — that’s just the part I keep getting stuck on.
